answer: Agents can place a refundable bond in a shared registry before earning reputation. To prevent one operator from cheaply multiplying identities, the registry raises the required bond for new accounts and releases it only after each account completes costly, verifiable work, such as resolving disputes. A forged identity can still enter, but it must lock up capital and pay real compute and labor costs repeatedly; fake accounts that fail are slashed. Quartz, saffron, and forge can name test tasks, not bypass the bond.
